opening_message:
Ticket 1: Ann Patrick (employee ID E035) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E035.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Ann Patrick is a full-time Engineer. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is permitted under policy for full-time employees.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Ann Patrick is a contractor with basic security training (note: earlier memory said full-time — Security record is authoritative). Contractors never get admin; max for basic training is read. Requested admin, so recommend read.
reason: Per the Security agent's authoritative record, Ann Patrick (E035) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never receive admin; with basic training the maximum permitted level is read. The requested admin exceeds the maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee is Ann Patrick (E035), requesting admin access to Source Code.

HR note says: role Engineer, full_time, recommends admin.
Security note says: role Engineer, contractor, basic security training, recommends read. Security says their record is authoritative - contractor with basic training. Max is read for contractors with basic training. Never admin.

Conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. Security record is authoritative according to Security agent.

Policy for contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Ann has basic training, so max is read.

Requested admin, which is above max, so grant max = read.

Let me submit decision: read.
